equipment.name: Resistance bands (generic light/medium set; no assumed poundages)
Doorway pull-up bar (in daddy's room; check it is secure every time)
Sturdy step stool on a non-slip floor

safety: A grown-up watches every session — strength nights and Tyler's Ten.
If anything hurts (sharp, pinchy, or ouchy — not just 'this is hard work'), stop right away and tell a grown-up.
Form comes before weight, reps, or going faster. A tidy set of 6 beats a sloppy set of 12.
Never swing, kip, or horse around on the pull-up bar.
Before any hang or band-on-the-bar move, a grown-up checks that the pull-up bar is tight and secure in the doorway.
Put the step stool on a non-slip floor, and have a grown-up stand close for step-ups and incline push-ups.
Leave 2 or 3 reps in the tank. We never go to failure — stop while the move still looks snappy.
No laundry baskets, chairs that roll, or wobbly benches. Floor, step stool, or the bar only.
notesForParent: This is fitness guidance only, not medical advice. If you have any concern about Tyler's health, pain, growth, or weight, check with his pediatrician.
Tyler is 9, lean, and already plays a lot of tennis. The plan stays short (20–25 minutes on lift nights) and never stacks two lifting days in a row.
Friday stays easy on his legs so he is fresh for Saturday's private lesson and Sunday matches.

He wanted to train every night, so Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday, and Sunday are Tyler's Ten: about 10 easy minutes of core, stretching, mobility, and balance — not another hard workout. After tennis is fine; skip any move that feels like too much that day.

The plan is fully doable with what you have now: a pair of 2 lb dumbbells, a generic light/medium resistance band set, the doorway pull-up bar, and a sturdy step stool. Progression uses reps, tempo, and harder bodyweight or band variations — not heavier loads he does not have yet.
If you buy a little more gear later, the plan notes where it can be swapped in. Do not jump more than one step at a time.

Double progression: only move to the next small step when every set hits the top of the rep range with clean form. If reps were missed or it felt hard, repeat the same target next time. Never jump more than one step.
Public files and the phone app use his first name only: Tyler.

recommendedPurchases.item: A few light dumbbell pairs (about 3, 5, and 8 lb)
recommendedPurchases.why: The 2 lb pair is perfect for learning curls, presses, and hinges. When Tyler owns the top of a rep range with tidy form, a slightly heavier pair is the next honest step — still kid-sized, not adult weights.
recommendedPurchases.swapIn: Goblet squats, Romanian deadlifts, curls, and overhead presses. Keep 2s for warm-up or slower tempo work.

recommendedPurchases.item: A mini-band loop set (light and medium)
recommendedPurchases.why: Small loops are great for sideways steps, glute activation, and knee tracking on squats — all tennis-friendly hip and landing strength — without tiring him out like extra running would.
recommendedPurchases.swapIn: Banded side steps on Tyler's Ten or Monday warm-ups, and a light loop above the knees on glute bridges or squats.

recommendedPurchases.why: A sturdy assist band lets Tyler practice a real pull-up pattern with his feet lightly helped, instead of only short hangs. Safer and more useful than trying to yank himself up.
recommendedPurchases.swapIn: Replace or follow the dead hang / scapular shrug work on Friday once a grown-up has fitted the band on the checked-secure bar.

split.why: Tyler has tennis class Tuesday and Thursday, a private lesson Saturday, and 2–3 hours of matches Sunday. Strength nights are Monday, Wednesday, and Friday so he never lifts two days in a row. Monday is the lower-body night because it sits farthest from the weekend matches. Wednesday is a full-body night with only easy lower work (glute bridges, not step-ups or hard squats) so he practices the hinge and core without loading tired tennis legs. Friday is upper only — no squats, step-ups, or hard calf work — so his legs stay fresh for Saturday and Sunday.

rules: Add the smallest available step only when every set hits the top of the rep range with clean form.
If reps were missed or it felt hard, repeat the same target next time.
Never jump more than one step.
A 'step' can be more reps inside the range, a slower tempo, a slightly harder bodyweight or band variation, or — later — the next light dumbbell pair if you buy one.
Never train to failure. Stop with 2 or 3 reps in the tank.

sections.title: Strength nights
sections.blurb: Monday, Wednesday, and Friday evenings, about 20 to 25 minutes.

sections.title: Tyler's Ten
sections.blurb: About 10 easy minutes after tennis (or in the evening). Light core, stretching, mobility, and balance. It should feel like a reset, not a workout. Skip any move that feels like too much that day.

checklist.target: Soft knee, long back, no bouncing.
Open up the shoulders after all those swings.
Tennis footwork balance. Use a wall if you wobble.

march-in-place.name: Easy march in place
cues: Soft quiet feet.
Swing the arms gently.
This is a warm-up, not a race.
march-in-place.videoTitle: DYNAMIC WARM UP March in Place updated

arm-circles.name: Arm circles
cues: Big slow circles.
Stand tall.
Reverse direction halfway.
arm-circles.videoTitle: DYNAMIC WARM UP Arm Circles updated

band-pull-apart.name: Band pull-apart
cues: Hold the band at chest height, soft elbows.
Pull the hands apart until the band touches the chest.
Squeeze the shoulder blades, then return slow.
band-pull-apart.videoTitle: How to Do Band Pull Aparts: A Guide from Physical Therapists

easy-squat-rehearsal.name: Easy squat rehearsal
cues: Sit back like a chair.
Toes forward, knees follow the toes.
Only go as low as you can stay tall.
easy-squat-rehearsal.videoTitle: How to do a body weight squat

bw-squat.name: Bodyweight squat
cues: Sit back, chest proud, heels stay down.
Knees track over the toes — they do not cave in.
Stand up tall at the top without leaning forward.
bw-squat.swapIn: A light goblet dumbbell (3–8 lb) once 2s feel very easy at the top of the range.
bw-squat.videoTitle: How to do a body weight squat

pause-squat.name: Pause squat
cues: Same tidy squat, then wait 2 seconds at the bottom.
Do not bounce.
Stand up without rushing.
pause-squat.swapIn: Goblet pause squat with a 3–8 lb dumbbell later.
pause-squat.videoTitle: How to do a body weight squat

goblet-squat-2lb.name: Goblet squat (2 lb)
cues: Hold one 2 lb dumbbell at the chest with both hands.
Sit back, elbows stay inside the knees.
Proud chest all the way up.
goblet-squat-2lb.swapIn: A 3, 5, or 8 lb dumbbell when every set hits the top of the range with clean form.
goblet-squat-2lb.videoTitle: How to do a Goblet Squat | Proper Form & Technique

tempo-goblet-squat-2lb.name: Slow goblet squat (2 lb)
cues: Count 3 seconds on the way down.
Gentle 1-second pause.
Stand up in 1 second, no bounce.
tempo-goblet-squat-2lb.swapIn: Same tempo with a slightly heavier goblet dumbbell later.
tempo-goblet-squat-2lb.videoTitle: How to do a Goblet Squat | Proper Form & Technique

hip-hinge.name: Hip hinge practice
cues: Soft knees, push the hips back like you are closing a car door.
Keep the back long and the chest proud.
You should feel it in the back of the legs, not the low back.
hip-hinge.videoTitle: DYNAMIC WARM UP Hip Hinges updated

rdl-2lb.name: Romanian deadlift (2 lb)
cues: Dumbbells slide down the front of the legs.
Hips back, back long, eyes on a spot on the floor a few feet ahead.
Squeeze the glutes to stand tall — do not lean back.
rdl-2lb.swapIn: Heavier light dumbbells (3–8 lb) once the 2s feel very easy with perfect hinges.
rdl-2lb.videoTitle: How to Do a Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift | Proper Form & Technique

pause-rdl-2lb.name: Pause Romanian deadlift (2 lb)
cues: Same hinge, pause 2 seconds at the bottom while the back stays long.
No rounding.
Stand tall with the glutes.
pause-rdl-2lb.swapIn: Pause RDLs with a slightly heavier pair later.
pause-rdl-2lb.videoTitle: How to Do a Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift | Proper Form & Technique

step-up.name: Step-up on the stool
cues: Whole foot on the stool, not just the toes.
Stand tall at the top, then step down slowly.
A grown-up stands close. Stool is on a non-slip floor.
step-up.swapIn: Hold 2s, then later a slightly heavier pair, once unweighted step-ups look easy.
step-up.videoTitle: Understanding Proper Step Up Form and Technique

slow-step-up.name: Slow step-down on the stool
cues: Step up as usual, then take 3 seconds to step down.
The standing leg does the work.
Grown-up close by, stool on a non-slip floor.
slow-step-up.swapIn: Add 2 lb dumbbells at the sides when the slow step-down is tidy.
slow-step-up.videoTitle: Understanding Proper Step Up Form and Technique

step-up-2lb.name: Step-up with 2 lb dumbbells
cues: Hold the 2s at your sides.
Whole foot on the stool, stand tall, step down slow.
Grown-up close by.
step-up-2lb.swapIn: A slightly heavier pair later — only after these look easy.
step-up-2lb.videoTitle: Understanding Proper Step Up Form and Technique

calf-raise.name: Calf raise
cues: Rise up on both feet, pause a moment at the top.
Lower slowly.
Hold a wall or a grown-up's hand if you need balance.
calf-raise.videoTitle: DYNAMIC WARM UP Calf Raises updated

calf-raise-step.name: Calf raise on the stool
cues: Balls of the feet on the stool, heels can dip a little, then rise high.
Hold a wall or grown-up for balance.
Stool on a non-slip floor. No bouncing.
calf-raise-step.videoTitle: DYNAMIC WARM UP Calf Raises updated

pause-calf-raise.name: Pause calf raise on the stool
cues: Same calf raise, squeeze 2 seconds at the top.
Lower slowly.
Hold on for balance.
pause-calf-raise.swapIn: Single-leg calf raises later, only when two-foot pauses are easy — and never to failure.
pause-calf-raise.videoTitle: DYNAMIC WARM UP Calf Raises updated

glute-bridge.name: Glute bridge
cues: Lie on your back, feet flat, knees bent.
Squeeze the glutes to lift the hips, not the low back.
Lower slowly.
glute-bridge.swapIn: A mini-band loop just above the knees later, if you buy a loop set.
glute-bridge.videoTitle: How to do a glute bridge

pause-glute-bridge.name: Pause glute bridge
cues: Same bridge, pause 2 seconds at the top.
Ribs stay down, squeeze the glutes.
Lower slowly.
pause-glute-bridge.videoTitle: How to do a glute bridge

incline-pushup.name: Incline push-up (hands on stool)
cues: Hands on the stool, body in a straight line from head to heels.
Elbows about 45 degrees, not flared out to a T.
Lower until the chest comes close, then press up. Stool on a non-slip floor.
incline-pushup.videoTitle: How to do an Incline Push-Up | Proper Form & Technique

tempo-incline-pushup.name: Slow incline push-up
cues: Same incline push-up, 3 seconds down, 1 second up.
Body stays a straight board.
Stop with 2 or 3 reps left.
tempo-incline-pushup.videoTitle: How to do an Incline Push-Up | Proper Form & Technique

knee-pushup.name: Knee push-up
cues: Hands under the shoulders, body straight from head to knees.
Lower with control, press up without sagging the hips.
If this gets sloppy, go back to incline push-ups.
knee-pushup.swapIn: Full push-ups later, only if every knee-push-up looks like a board — and never to failure.
knee-pushup.videoTitle: How to do a Modified Push-Up | Proper Form & Technique

band-row.name: Band row
cues: Loop the band over the checked-secure pull-up bar.
Pull the elbows back, squeeze the shoulder blades, stand tall.
Return slow. No leaning way back.
band-row.swapIn: A slightly thicker band, or later a one-arm dumbbell row with a 3–8 lb weight, hand supported on the stool.
band-row.videoTitle: How to do a Standing Tubing Row

pause-band-row.name: Pause band row
cues: Same row, pause 2 seconds when the hands are by the ribs.
Squeeze the shoulder blades.
Return slow.
pause-band-row.swapIn: One-arm dumbbell rows later if you buy slightly heavier dumbbells.
pause-band-row.videoTitle: How to do a Standing Tubing Row

oh-press-2lb.name: Overhead press (2 lb)
cues: Start with the dumbbells at the shoulders.
Press straight up, head stays neutral, ribs stay down (no big back arch).
Lower slowly to the shoulders.
oh-press-2lb.swapIn: A 3 or 5 lb pair once the 2s are very easy at the top of the range.
oh-press-2lb.videoTitle: How to do a Dumbbell Overhead Press

pause-oh-press-2lb.name: Pause overhead press (2 lb)
cues: Same press, pause 1–2 seconds at the top without shrugging the ears.
Ribs down.
Lower slowly.
pause-oh-press-2lb.videoTitle: How to do a Dumbbell Overhead Press

curl-2lb.name: Biceps curl (2 lb)
cues: Elbows stay by the sides — no swinging.
Curl up, squeeze, lower slowly.
Have fun with these — they are in the plan on purpose.
curl-2lb.swapIn: A 3 or 5 lb pair once every set hits the top of the range with no swing.

tempo-curl-2lb.name: Slow biceps curl (2 lb)
cues: Curl up in 1 second, lower in 3 seconds.
No swinging the torso.
Elbows stay by the sides.
tempo-curl-2lb.swapIn: Same slow tempo with a slightly heavier pair later.

dead-hang-supported.name: Supported dead hang
cues: Grown-up checks the bar first.
Hold the bar, keep both feet on the floor or a stool so you can stand anytime.
Bend the knees a little to let the arms feel a gentle hang. No swinging. Stand up whenever you want.
dead-hang-supported.swapIn: A pull-up assist band can follow this, once a grown-up fits it on the checked-secure bar.

scapular-shrug.name: Scapular shrug on the bar
cues: Grown-up checks the bar first.
From a gentle supported hang, pull the shoulders down and together without bending the elbows much.
Relax, then repeat. Feet stay close to the floor. No swinging.
scapular-shrug.swapIn: Assist-band pull-ups later, after these look easy and calm.

dead-bug.name: Dead bug
cues: Back flat on the floor, arms up, knees bent over the hips.
Slowly reach one arm back and the opposite leg out, then return.
If the low back pops up, make the move smaller.
dead-bug.videoTitle: How to do a Dead Bug | Proper Form & Technique

bird-dog.name: Bird dog
cues: Hands and knees, back like a table.
Slide one arm forward and the opposite leg back, pause, return.
Hips stay level — no tipping.
bird-dog.videoTitle: How to do a Bird Dog | Proper Form & Technique

kneeling-plank.name: Kneeling plank
cues: Elbows under the shoulders, knees down, body in a straight line to the knees.
Squeeze the glutes, do not let the hips sag or pike up.
Breathe. Stop while it still looks tidy.
kneeling-plank.videoTitle: How To Plank From Knee (Modified Plank)

cat-cow.name: Cat-cow
cues: Hands and knees.
Slowly round the back, then gently look up and soften the belly.
Easy breathing, no forcing.
cat-cow.videoTitle: COOL DOWN Cat Cow Stretch updated

hip-flexor-stretch.name: Hip flexor stretch
cues: Half-kneeling, tuck the pelvis slightly, gentle shift forward.
You should feel the front of the back-leg hip.
Switch sides. No pain.
hip-flexor-stretch.videoTitle: How to do a hip flexor stretch

hamstring-stretch.name: Hamstring stretch
cues: One heel out, soft knee, hinge forward a little.
Long back, no bouncing.
Switch sides.
hamstring-stretch.videoTitle: How to Do a Standing Hamstring Stretch: A Guide from Physical Therapists

chest-opener.name: Chest and shoulder opener
cues: Stand in a doorway or clasp hands behind you and lift gently.
Easy stretch, breathe.
Shoulders stay relaxed.

single-leg-balance.name: Single-leg balance
cues: Stand tall on one foot, soft knee, eyes on a spot.
Switch sides.
Use a wall if you wobble — tennis balance, not a contest.
single-leg-balance.videoTitle: Single Leg Balance - Ask Doctor Jo

calf-stretch.name: Calf stretch
cues: Hands on a wall, one foot back, heel down.
Gentle and still.
Switch sides.
calf-stretch.videoTitle: How to do a calf (gastrocnemius) stretch

easy-breathing.name: Easy belly breaths
cues: Lie on your back or sit tall.
Breathe in through the nose, feel the belly rise, slow breath out.
This is the cool-down — no rushing.
